title: Humanoid robots pummel a YouTuber in cage matches and California tells the startup to stop the fights
source_used: Tom's Hardware (4 Oct 2026, full article read; it quotes the letter and embeds REK CEO Cix Liv's X posts); TechSpot (full text from the fulltext folder), PCMag UK, Fox News (the CyberGuy column by Kurt Knutsson) and GIGAZINE read in full; NBC News's 18-second video short of 3 Oct has no text and the CyberGuy original returned 403
key_facts: California's state athletic commission (CSAC) sent REK, a robot-fighting startup, a cease-and-desist letter; REK founder and CEO Cix Liv shared it on X on 30 Sep 2026 with the words 'We made it boys' (Tom's Hardware; TechSpot also dates the letter 30 Sep).

The letter orders REK to stop (1) holding, promoting or advertising any boxing or mixed martial arts contest, match or exhibition involving any human in California without the commission's prior approval, and (2) promoting or taking part in one without a licence; it adds that Business and Professions Code sections 18870 and 18878 make holding such a contest without a licence or permit a misdemeanour (Tom's Hardware, quoting the letter).

The letter refers to a human-versus-humanoid cage fight that REK sponsored on 18 Sep 2026 in San Francisco, in which YouTuber Frankie LaPenna faced three different robots (Tom's Hardware; GIGAZINE gives the same date and city and says LaPenna posted the video on 20 Sep).

Fox News (Kurt Knutsson's CyberGuy column), citing REK's technology partner Reflex Arc, says human pilots steer the robots in real time with VR gear or a gamepad while AI helps with balance and trained movement; PCMag UK and GIGAZINE also say the robots were remotely controlled. Fox lists LaPenna's opponents as a Unitree G1 and two modified EngineAI T800 robots, about 6 ft tall.

Accounts of the bout differ: TechSpot describes a kick to the face that sent LaPenna into the cage, a kick to the stomach that put him on his back and punches that put him on the ground; PCMag UK says he reportedly won every fight and lost only one round; Fox says he was knocked down in one bout and, per Liv, ended it with the robot's head coming off.

Tom's Hardware says it is unclear whether the fight was a sporting contest or a promotional stunt, and that the letter's wording suggests the commission would not have intervened in a robot-only fight; GIGAZINE says the order applies to matches involving humans, there is no confirmation it covers robot-only matches, and REK's website still advertises robot fighting events.

Fox, citing Liv, says LaPenna wore motorcycle-style protective gear and gloves at REK's insistence and hurt a hand but was otherwise not seriously hurt; REK advertises 'Real pilots, real punches' and offers private events from $10,000 (Tom's Hardware).
quote_evidence: A robotics startup just received a cease-and-desist letter from the state of California after it hosted a human vs. robot fight in San Francisco.

The cease-and-desist refers to the human vs. humanoid cage fight that the company sponsored on Sep. 18, 2026, where YouTuber Frankie LaPenna entered a fighting cage and faced off with three different robots.
REK's technology partner Reflex Arc says pilots operate the humanoids in real time using VR gear or a gamepad.
why_it_matters_hint: California's athletic commission says a fight between a person and a robot needs its approval and a licence; the robots were steered by human pilots and accounts differ on how the fight went.
event_date: Fight on 18 Sep 2026 in San Francisco (LaPenna posted video on 20 Sep); letter and Liv's X post on 30 Sep 2026; Tom's Hardware reported it on 4 Oct 2026 and TechSpot, PCMag UK, Fox News and GIGAZINE on 5 Oct 2026
notes: Credit: the pool item is TechSpot, which names no source. PCMag UK ('As Tom's Hardware reports') and GIGAZINE (cites Tom's Hardware) both name Tom's Hardware as the origin, and Tom's Hardware (4 Oct 2026, Jowi Morales) is the first full written report of the letter that I found, quoting it and embedding Liv's X posts, so it is credited and linked. NBC News ran an 18-second video short on the letter on 3 Oct (no text to read). Fox News carries Kurt Knutsson's CyberGuy column (copyright CyberGuy.com; the original at cyberguy.com returned 403). The story is older than the window: fight 18 Sep, letter 30 Sep, and our own pools carried it earlier (3 Oct pool C16-05, CyberGuy, published 2 Oct; 4 Oct pool C11-10, NBC News video, published 3 Oct, score 4), neither printed in the archived 3 to 5 Oct Full Reports. Small differences: TechSpot says 'Last month' where Tom's Hardware and GIGAZINE give 18 Sep; TechSpot says the commission sent the letter on 30 Sep while Tom's Hardware dates Liv's post 30 Sep; the outcome accounts differ (see key facts); TechSpot does not say the robots were piloted. Tom's Hardware's view that the commission would not have intervened in a robot-only fight is its own reading of the letter.
